evidence.quote: let statement (customerId: string) (currency: string) (from: DateOnly) (until: DateOnly) (r: Receivables) : Result<Statement, string> =
|> List.sortBy (fun l -> l.Date, (if l.Kind = Invoiced then 0 else 1), l.Invoice)
match books.Books.Customers.TryFind customerId, Statements.statement customerId "USD" from until books with

ARC-REV-01.rationale: All of the statement's meaning (which invoices count, the line kinds, the issue-date clamp, the ordering, opening, running balance, closing and the error cases) is in Tier 1 Summa.Ledger.Statements and is built on Payments.settlement. The Tier 2 engine checks the range with the existing dateRange and the capability with the existing mayExportOn, then calls Statements.statement. The Tier 3 wire only maps the kernel event to the engine message. No Tier 3/4 code re-decides anything.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No clock, randomness, file, network or console effect is added below Tier 4. 'Today' comes from model.Today, and the download is asked for as data (an OfferDownload engine effect) for the kernel to carry out. One thing to note: the Tier 2 Storage serializer uses an in-memory IO.MemoryStream and Text.Json.Utf8JsonWriter. That conflicts with the symbol rule ARC-SYM-01, but it is pure, deterministic serialization and not an external effect, so it does not lower the effect-flow score.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The statement facts each have one definition: the kind names in statementKind, schema and version in StatementSchema/StatementVersion, Classification reused, and the export capability through the existing mayExportOn branch. Two formatting facts are copied, though the copies agree. The engine defines its own 'iso' date format instead of using the one Exports already has. statementJson writes money with a local {currency, minor} writer instead of reusing the invoice document's writer, which the requirement names as the reference.

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The aging split is computed in Tier 1 Statements. It reuses the existing Payments.bucket and the same invoiceLines that build the statement, so the parts agree with Closing by construction. The CSV layout is Tier 2 Storage, built on the existing Exports.withHeader and Reports.csvField. The engine (Tier 2) chooses JSON or CSV and gets the data version from Exports.dataVersion. The Tier 3 wire change is one event mapping. No rule is decided in Tier 3/4.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The 'generated' time comes from the per-message Ctx.Now that the composition root supplies, not from a clock read. The CSV is offered as an OfferDownload effect value for Tier 4 to carry out. No new effect enters Tier 1/2/3.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The aging buckets, csvField, statementKind and the export header all point back to their single definitions. The CSV amount formatter is new and local, though: it hard-codes a minor-unit scale of 100 and two decimal places instead of using an existing money or report amount formatter. It agrees for USD, which is the only currency offered. The engine's local copy of the yyyy-MM-dd date format is kept and now also names the CSV file. These are copies that agree, not contradictions.
